3038:311.name: Chart
3038:311.description:
Chart is a flexible data-visualization component with 12 variants for comparing values, revealing trends, showing composition, and communicating progress.

WHEN TO USE
Use charts when a visual pattern, relationship, distribution, or change is easier to understand than a table of raw values. Choose the Type variant that best matches the analytical question and data structure.

USAGE GUIDELINES
• Use a clear, outcome-focused title and a short description that explains scope, timeframe, or unit.
• Choose the simplest chart type that communicates the insight accurately.
• Keep category count, series count, labels, and legends concise.
• Use consistent colors for the same metric across related views.
• Enable grid lines and data labels only when they improve interpretation.
• Do not use charts for a single value when a KPI or statistic component is clearer.
• Provide an accessible text summary or data table when the chart contains critical information.

PROPERTIES
• Type: Bar, Line, Area, Donut, Pie, Stacked Bar, Horizontal Bar, Scatter, Radar, Gauge, Funnel, or Waterfall.
• Show Title: Shows or hides the chart title.
• Show Description: Shows or hides supporting context beneath the title.
• Show Legend: Shows or hides the series or category legend.
• Show Grid Lines: Shows or hides chart reference lines.
• Show Data Labels: Shows or hides values attached to data marks.
• Title Text: Overrides the default chart title.
• Description Text: Overrides the default supporting description.
• Content: Accepts optional custom content for the selected chart variant.

3038:308.name: Type=Bar
3038:308.description:
Vertical bar chart for comparing discrete categories or values across periods.

WHEN TO USE
Use when the main task is comparing category magnitudes or a small number of time periods.

USAGE GUIDELINES
• Start the value axis at zero to avoid exaggerating differences.
• Keep category labels short and use a consistent order.
• Use one series when possible; group bars only when direct comparison is necessary.
• Switch to Horizontal Bar when labels are long or there are many categories.

PROPERTIES
• Type: Bar.
• Supports all shared visibility, text, legend, grid-line, data-label, and content properties.

3038:309.name: Type=Line
3038:309.description:
Line chart for visualizing trends and change across a continuous sequence.

WHEN TO USE
Use for time-series data or ordered intervals where continuity and direction matter.

USAGE GUIDELINES
• Keep intervals evenly spaced and chronological.
• Limit the number of lines so each series remains distinguishable.
• Use data labels selectively; prioritize endpoints, peaks, or notable events.
• Do not use for unrelated categories with no meaningful order.

PROPERTIES
• Type: Line.
• Supports all shared visibility, text, legend, grid-line, data-label, and content properties.

3038:310.name: Type=Area
3038:310.description:
Area chart that emphasizes both trend and magnitude with a filled region.

WHEN TO USE
Use for continuous data when total volume or cumulative magnitude is as important as the trend.

USAGE GUIDELINES
• Use transparent fills when multiple series overlap.
• Keep the baseline at zero when area represents quantity.
• Avoid too many overlapping series because the fill can obscure values.
• Use Line when precise comparison matters more than volume.

PROPERTIES
• Type: Area.
• Supports all shared visibility, text, legend, grid-line, data-label, and content properties.

3040:21573.name: Type=Donut
3040:21573.description:
Donut chart for showing part-to-whole relationships with an optional summary value in the center.

WHEN TO USE
Use for a small set of mutually exclusive categories that add up to a meaningful whole.

USAGE GUIDELINES
• Limit the number of segments and order them consistently.
• Place the key total or primary metric in the center when useful.
• Avoid similar colors and very small slices.
• Use Bar when users need precise comparisons.

PROPERTIES
• Type: Donut.
• Supports all shared visibility, text, legend, data-label, and content properties; grid lines may not apply visually.

3040:21574.name: Type=Pie
3040:21574.description:
Pie chart for communicating a simple proportional distribution across categories.

WHEN TO USE
Use only when categories form a complete whole and approximate share is the primary message.

USAGE GUIDELINES
• Keep the slice count low and sort by value where appropriate.
• Begin the largest slice from a consistent reference position.
• Avoid 3D effects and exploded slices.
• Use Donut for a center summary or Bar for precise comparison.

PROPERTIES
• Type: Pie.
• Supports all shared visibility, text, legend, data-label, and content properties; grid lines may not apply visually.

3040:21575.name: Type=Stacked Bar
3040:21575.description:
Stacked bar chart for comparing totals and their internal composition across categories.

WHEN TO USE
Use when both the overall amount and contribution of sub-categories are important.

USAGE GUIDELINES
• Keep segment order and colors consistent across every bar.
• Limit the number of segments to preserve readability.
• Use a 100% stacked treatment only when comparing proportions rather than totals.
• Use grouped Bar when each segment requires precise comparison.

PROPERTIES
• Type: Stacked Bar.
• Supports all shared visibility, text, legend, grid-line, data-label, and content properties.

3040:21576.name: Type=Horizontal Bar
3040:21576.description:
Horizontal bar chart for comparing or ranking categories, especially when labels are long.

WHEN TO USE
Use for rankings, survey responses, or category names that need more horizontal space.

USAGE GUIDELINES
• Sort bars intentionally, usually highest to lowest for rankings.
• Start the value axis at zero.
• Keep labels left-aligned and easy to scan.
• Use vertical Bar when category labels are short and period comparison is more natural.

PROPERTIES
• Type: Horizontal Bar.
• Supports all shared visibility, text, legend, grid-line, data-label, and content properties.

3043:283.name: Type=Scatter
3043:283.description:
Scatter plot for revealing relationships, distributions, clusters, and outliers between two quantitative variables.

WHEN TO USE
Use when investigating correlation or how two numeric measures vary together.

USAGE GUIDELINES
• Label both axes with units and meaningful scales.
• Use color or shape for a limited number of additional groups.
• Add a trend line only when it supports the analytical purpose.
• Do not imply causation from correlation alone.

PROPERTIES
• Type: Scatter.
• Supports all shared visibility, text, legend, grid-line, data-label, and content properties.

3043:284.name: Type=Radar
3043:284.description:
Radar chart for comparing multiple quantitative dimensions across one or a few entities.

WHEN TO USE
Use for compact performance profiles when every dimension shares a comparable scale.

USAGE GUIDELINES
• Keep the number of axes and compared entities low.
• Use the same range and direction for every axis.
• Arrange related dimensions together.
• Use grouped Bar when accurate cross-dimension comparison is critical.

PROPERTIES
• Type: Radar.
• Supports all shared visibility, text, legend, grid-line, data-label, and content properties.

3043:285.name: Type=Gauge
3043:285.description:
Gauge chart for showing one metric relative to a target, threshold, or bounded range.

WHEN TO USE
Use in KPI dashboards when progress or status must be understood at a glance.

USAGE GUIDELINES
• Define the minimum, maximum, target, and threshold meaning clearly.
• Use color semantically and avoid decorative ranges.
• Show the exact value alongside the visual indicator.
• Use a progress bar or KPI when space or precision is more important.

PROPERTIES
• Type: Gauge.
• Supports shared title, description, legend, data-label, and content properties; grid lines may not apply visually.

3043:286.name: Type=Funnel
3043:286.description:
Funnel chart for visualizing values across sequential stages in a process.

WHEN TO USE
Use for conversion, onboarding, recruitment, or sales pipelines where each stage follows the previous one.

USAGE GUIDELINES
• Keep stages in their true process order.
• Show both count and conversion rate when useful.
• Explain unexpected increases between stages.
• Use Bar when the categories are not sequential.

PROPERTIES
• Type: Funnel.
• Supports shared title, description, legend, data-label, and content properties; grid lines may not apply visually.

3043:287.name: Type=Waterfall
3043:287.description:
Waterfall chart for explaining how sequential positive and negative changes produce a final value.

WHEN TO USE
Use for financial bridges, budget variance, inventory movement, or any additive change analysis.

USAGE GUIDELINES
• Distinguish increases, decreases, subtotals, and totals consistently.
• Label the starting and ending values clearly.
• Keep the sequence chronological or logically causal.
• Use Bar when values are independent rather than cumulative.

PROPERTIES
• Type: Waterfall.
• Supports all shared visibility, text, legend, grid-line, data-label, and content properties.
